comments.author: @StockSmartU
comments.text:
I’m Bulgarian, and this honestly doesn’t make much sense to me. The correct and natural way to write it in Bulgarian would be „Разходка с лодка по канала.“

That said, I’m not particularly surprised by the wording, given the history and linguistic similarities between Bulgarian and Macedonian.

As for the title of your video, “How similar is Bulgarian to Macedonian?” — the relationship between the two languages is much more complicated than simply saying they are separate, unrelated languages. Macedonian developed within the same South Slavic linguistic continuum as Bulgarian, and there are significant similarities between the two.

The Cyrillic script itself was developed in the medieval Bulgarian cultural sphere, particularly at the Preslav Literary School, and Bulgaria played a central role in its development and spread.

So, to put it simply: Bulgarian and Macedonian are extremely closely related languages with a shared history, and the origins and development of the Cyrillic alphabet are deeply connected to medieval Bulgaria.
